prompt: Who reports the outcome figures on an AVEVA success-story page?

options.text: AVEVA, the vendor; they are not independently audited

explanation: A success story is a vendor-published customer case. Its outcomes are as reported by AVEVA and are not independently audited.

prompt: How should this figure be described?
scenario: A 2015 OSIsoft seminar deck says DONG Energy could "cut OPEX by up to about €20M per year (NPV)" with condition-based and predictive monitoring of 1,800 offshore turbines.

options.text: As an expectation, reported by OSIsoft, not a measured result
As a figure DONG Energy's auditors confirmed

explanation: "could" and "up to about" mark an expectation. The research notes it is an expectation, not a measured result, reported in an OSIsoft deck.

prompt: Which of these AVEVA stories were checked and found NOT to use the PI System? Select all that apply.
explanation: Nestlé Waverly (AVEVA Historian, CONNECT), Henkel (MES, System Platform) and City of Bremen (InTouch, Historian) are not PI System stories. Covestro and Illovo are.

prompt: True or false: The 2026 "last published" date on an AVEVA success-story page tells you the project year.
explanation: False. AVEVA success-story pages show only a 2026 "last published" date, which is not the project year. Treat the year as not stated unless the text gives one.

prompt: Match each case-study figure to who reported it.

pairs.left: Luminant: $160K saved on its latest combined-cycle unit
pairs.right: The company, at a 2017 OSIsoft regional seminar
Capula Ltd, in an OSIsoft EMEA 2014 presentation
Mipac, an integrator, in a 2025 article
OSIsoft, at a 2014 São Paulo regional seminar

explanation: Each figure's reporter comes from the cs.library entry. Who reports a figure affects how much weight to give it.

prompt: Which words in a case study signal that a figure is NOT a measured result? Select all that apply.
explanation: "Expected" (Detroit, UC Davis), "Projected" (UC Davis), "roughly estimated" (Xcel) and "on track for" (Covestro) all mark forecasts, estimates or targets. "Reduced" usually reports a result.

prompt: Which sentence is the honest rewrite?
scenario: A slide says "PI saved Xcel $46M." The AVEVA story quotes Kasen Huwa of Xcel Energy: "Savings and efficiencies are roughly estimated over the last six years at $46 million".

options.text: Xcel Energy estimates savings and efficiencies of roughly $46 million over six years (Kasen Huwa, Xcel Energy, in an AVEVA success story)
Xcel Energy saved $46M in one year

explanation: Keep the hedge (roughly estimated), the period (six years), the scope (savings and efficiencies) and the reporter. Rounding, annualising or shortening the period all change the claim.

prompt: Why is CSL Group's "8,233 mt CO2e avoided across 11 vessels in a year" stronger evidence than most success-story figures?

options.text: The source says it was third-party verified
It is the largest figure in the library
It was measured on every vessel in the fleet

explanation: The research notes the CSL CO2e figure is third-party verified. Most success-story outcomes are reported by AVEVA without independent checks. It covers 11 vessels, not CSL's whole fleet of over 40.

prompt: Which qualifiers must you keep when quoting this?
scenario: Noble Energy said in its own OSIsoft seminar presentation that using PI during the Aseng FPSO startup helped engineers increase production by an estimated 10,000 barrels of oil per day.

options.text: None; it is a precise figure
Convert it to barrels per year for clarity

explanation: It is the company's own estimate, presented at a vendor seminar. Keep both qualifiers. Do not convert units.

prompt: PI Academy's case-study library holds ___ PI System case studies, all with readable sources.
explanation: The research built 83 PI System case blocks, all with readable sources, and separately listed AVEVA stories that do not use PI.

prompt: Who usually presents a case at PI World or AVEVA World, and so reports its figures?

options.text: The customer company or its integrator, sometimes OSIsoft/AVEVA staff

explanation: PI World / AVEVA World is the user conference where customers present their PI deployments; some decks are given by OSIsoft staff (for example the 2014 Pertamina figures).

prompt: True or false: OSIsoft's claim that PI is used by "95% of the Global Fortune Top 40 oil and gas companies" is an independently verified market statistic.
explanation: False. It comes from OSIsoft's own 2023 company overview, and the research notes the page's labels were scrambled, so even the pairing of figure and industry is a best interpretation.

prompt: Some case studies, such as Nutrien, LADWP and Cargill, state no outcome figures. What should you do?

options.text: Describe what they built and say no figures are stated
Borrow a typical figure from a similar company
Estimate a figure from the tag count
Leave them out of all training

explanation: Qualitative stories are still useful for architecture and use cases. Never invent or borrow figures; say that none are stated.

prompt: Order the checks to make before reusing a case-study figure.

items.text: Confirm the story uses the PI System
Find the exact wording in the source
Identify whether it is a result, estimate, expectation or target
Quote it exactly with its reporter

explanation: Start by checking it is a PI story at all, then read the exact words, note the reporter and the kind of figure, and finally quote it exactly with attribution.
